title.en: Ampère's circuital law and the solenoid

hook.en: Gauss's law made symmetric electric problems easy. Ampère's *circuital* law does the same for magnetism: walk once round a closed loop, and the field along it tells you the current inside.
hook.kn: ಗಾಸ್ ನಿಯಮ ಸಮಮಿತ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ಸುಲಭಗೊಳಿಸಿತು. ಆಂಪಿಯರ್‌ನ ಆವರ್ತ ನಿಯಮ ಕಾಂತತ್ವಕ್ಕೆ ಅದೇ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Gauss's law made symmetric electric problems easy. Ampère's circuital law does the same for magnetism: walk once round a closed loop, and the field along it tells you the current inside. In this lesson: State Ampère's circuital law and use it for a long straight wire.
Find the field inside a long solenoid.

body.en: The line integral of B around any closed loop equals μ₀ times the current threading the loop: $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 I_{enc}$. For a long straight wire, take a circle of radius r: $B\cdot2\pi r = \mu_0I$, so $B = \mu_0I/2\pi r$. The field lines are concentric circles around the wire; the right-hand thumb rule gives their sense.
body.kn: ಆಂಪಿಯರ್ ನಿಯಮ: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_ಒಳಗೆ. ಉದ್ದ ನೇರ ತಂತಿಗೆ B = μ₀I/2πr; ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ತಂತಿಯ ಸುತ್ತ ಏಕಕೇಂದ್ರೀಯ ವೃತ್ತಗಳು.

narration.en: Ampère's law says the sum of B along a closed loop equals mu nought times the current inside. For a long straight wire this gives B equals mu nought I by 2 pi r, in circles around the wire.
narration.kn: ಆಂಪಿಯರ್ ನಿಯಮ: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_ಒಳಗೆ. ಉದ್ದ ನೇರ ತಂತಿಗೆ B = μ₀I/2πr; ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ತಂತಿಯ ಸುತ್ತ ಏಕಕೇಂದ್ರೀಯ ವೃತ್ತಗಳು.

blocks.formula: \oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 I_{enc},\qquad B_{wire} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}

say.en: Ampère's law says the sum of B along a closed loop equals mu nought times the current inside. For a long straight wire this gives B equals mu nought I by 2 pi r, in circles around the wire. ∮B dl equals micro 0I enc.

say.en: Long wire: B equals micro 0I/2 pi r.

title.en: On the board: Ampère's law: wire and solenoid

narration.en: Round a long straight wire the field lines are circles, and B is the same all round a circle of radius r. Take one circle as the Amperian loop: B × 2πr = μ₀I, so B = μ₀I/2πr. Example: 5 A at 4 cm from the wire gives B = 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 5 / 0.04 = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ T. In a long solenoid the field inside is uniform and along the axis; outside it is nearly zero. Ampère's law on the rectangle gives B L = μ₀ n L I, so B = μ₀ n I. Example: 500 turns on 0.5 m carrying 5 A: n = 1000 per metre, so B ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻³ T.

Take one circle as the Amperian loop: B × 2πr = μ₀I, so B = μ₀I/2πr.
Example: 5 A at 4 cm from the wire gives B = 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 5 / 0.04 = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ T.
In a long solenoid the field inside is uniform and along the axis; outside it is nearly zero.
Ampère's law on the rectangle gives B L = μ₀ n L I, so B = μ₀ n I.
Example: 500 turns on 0.5 m carrying 5 A: n = 1000 per metre, so B ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻³ T.

Round a long straight wire the field lines are circles, and B is the same all round a circle of radius r. Take one circle as the Amperian loop: B times 2 pi r equals micro 0I, so B equals micro 0I/2 pi r. Example: 5 A at 4 centimetres from the wire gives B equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times 5 divided by 0.04 equals 2.5 times 10 to the power minus 5 T. In a long solenoid the field inside is uniform and along the axis; outside it is nearly zero. Ampère's law on the rectangle gives B L equals micro 0 n L I, so B equals micro 0 n I. Example: 500 turns on 0.5 metres carrying 5 A: n equals 1000 per metre, so B is approximately 6.3 times 10 to the power minus 3 T.

narration.en: Ampère's law applied to a rectangular loop gives B = μ0 n I inside a long solenoid, where n is turns per metre; outside, the field is almost zero. Drag the probe: the field is uniform in the middle and falls to about half at the ends. Solenoid: 40 cm long, radius 4 cm.

body.en: A long *solenoid* with n turns per unit length carrying current I has a uniform field inside, along its axis: $B = \mu_0nI$. Outside, the field is nearly zero. At the ends the field is about half the value at the middle. A soft-iron core greatly increases B.

aim.en: To study how the strength of an electromagnet depends on the number of turns, the current and the core. Try this: A coil on a nail is a short solenoid with an iron core. Double the current, then the number of turns, and count the pins each time: the field grows with nI, as B = μ₀nI says, and the iron core makes it far stronger than a wooden one.
aim.kn: ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ಕಾಂತದ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸುತ್ತುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಮತ್ತು ತಿರುಳಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಅಧ್ಯಯನ ಮಾಡುವುದು. ಇದನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ: ಮೊಳೆಯ ಮೇಲಿನ ಸುರುಳಿ ಕಬ್ಬಿಣದ ತಿರುಳಿರುವ ಒಂದು ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಸೊಲೆನಾಯ್ಡ್. ಪ್ರವಾಹವನ್ನು, ನಂತರ ಸುತ್ತುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ದ್ವಿಗುಣಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಬಾರಿ ಪಿನ್ನುಗಳನ್ನು ಎಣಿಸಿ: B = μ₀nI ಹೇಳುವಂತೆ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ nI ಜೊತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ; ಕಬ್ಬಿಣದ ತಿರುಳು ಮರದ ತಿರುಳಿಗಿಂತ ಅದನ್ನು ಬಹಳ ಪ್ರಬಲಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

tagline.en: Calculating magnetic fields of wires, loops, solenoids and toroids.

say.en: Biot–Savart: $dB \propto I\,dl\sin\theta/r^2$.
Wire $\mu_0 I/2\pi r$; loop centre $\mu_0 NI/2R$; solenoid $\mu_0 nI$; toroid $\mu_0 NI/2\pi r$.
Ampère's law $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 I_{enc}$ is useful only with high symmetry.
On the axis far from a loop, B falls as 1/x³ — the loop is a magnetic dipole.

problem.en: A long straight wire carries 5 A. Find the magnetic field 10 cm from it.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A long straight wire carries 5 A. Find the magnetic field 10 cm from it.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A long straight wire carries 5 A. Find the magnetic field 10 centimetres from it.
B equals micro 0I/2 pi r equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times I over r.
B equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times 5 over 0.1.
B equals 1 times 10 to the power minus 5 T.
So the answer is 1 times 10 to the power minus 5 T.

problem.en: A solenoid 0.5 m long has 500 turns and carries 5 A. Find the field inside it.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A solenoid 0.5 m long has 500 turns and carries 5 A. Find the field inside it.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A solenoid 0.5 metres long has 500 turns and carries 5 A. Find the field inside it.
n equals 500 over 0.5 equals 1000 turns m to the power minus 1.
B equals micro 0nI equals 4 pi times 10 to the power minus 7 times 1000 times 5.
B is approximately 6.28 times 10 to the power minus 3 T.
So the answer is About 6.28 times 10 to the power minus 3 T.

body.en: Since μ₀/4π = 10⁻⁷, the field of a long wire is B = 2 × 10⁻⁷ I/r, and the force per metre between two wires is 2 × 10⁻⁷ I₁I₂/d. No π to carry around.

say.en: The 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 shortcut. Since micro 0 over 4 pi equals 10 to the power minus 7, the field of a long wire is B equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 I over r, and the force per metre between two wires is 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 I 1I 2 over d. homework.en: A solenoid of length 0.4 m with 2000 turns carries 2 A. Find the field inside it.

narration.en: Recap. Ampère: ∮B · dl = μ₀I_enc. Long wire: B = μ₀I/2πr = 2 × 10⁻⁷ I/r. Solenoid: B = μ₀nI inside, nearly zero outside.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಆಂಪಿಯರ್: ∮B · dl = μ₀I_ಒಳಗೆ. ಉದ್ದ ತಂತಿ: B = μ₀I/2πr = 2 × 10⁻⁷ I/r. ಸೊಲೆನಾಯ್ಡ್: ಒಳಗೆ B = μ₀nI, ಹೊರಗೆ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

answers.en: B = μ₀nI inside, nearly zero outside.
answers.kn: ಒಳಗೆ B = μ₀nI, ಹೊರಗೆ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

title.en: Force between two parallel currents; the ampere
title.kn: ಎರಡು ಸಮಾಂತರ ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ಬಲ; ಆಂಪಿಯರ್

say.en: Can you recall these? Ampère:? ∮B dl equals micro 0I enc.
say.kn: ಇವುಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಬಲ್ಲಿರಾ? ಆಂಪಿಯರ್:? ∮B dl equals micro 0I ಒಳಗೆ.

say.en: Long wire:? B equals micro 0I/2 pi r equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 I over r.
say.kn: ಉದ್ದ ತಂತಿ:? B equals micro 0I/2 pi r equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 I over r.

say.en: Solenoid:? B equals micro 0nI inside, nearly zero outside.
say.kn: ಸೊಲೆನಾಯ್ಡ್:? ಒಳಗೆ B equals micro 0nI, ಹೊರಗೆ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಶೂನ್ಯ.
